# WW2 Film Map

> Bilingual interactive guide to the cinema of the world wars: 222 films and
> series about the First World War, the interwar years, and the Second World
> War, placed on a 3D globe with historical borders, fronts, and events.

English: https://ww2.stevenacz.com/
Spanish: https://ww2.stevenacz.com/es/
Source code: https://github.com/StevenACZ/ww2-movie-map
Sitemap: https://ww2.stevenacz.com/sitemap_index.xml

## Key pages

- Globe map: https://ww2.stevenacz.com/
- Films and series: https://ww2.stevenacz.com/films/
- World War I era: https://ww2.stevenacz.com/era/ww1/
- Interwar era: https://ww2.stevenacz.com/era/interwar/
- World War II era: https://ww2.stevenacz.com/era/ww2/
- Places: https://ww2.stevenacz.com/places/
- Timeline: https://ww2.stevenacz.com/timeline/
- About and credits: https://ww2.stevenacz.com/about/

Every page has a Spanish version under /es/ (for example
https://ww2.stevenacz.com/es/films/). Title pages live at /films/{id}/ and
place pages at /places/{id}/, where a title id is a slug followed by the
release year.

## What the data covers

- 222 titles: 202 films and 20 series; 27 set in WW1, 25 in the interwar
  years, and 170 in WW2, across Western and Eastern Europe, the
  Mediterranean, the Atlantic, the Pacific, Asia, and the Americas.
- A curated set of must-watch classics, marked in gold.
- For each title: bilingual synopsis and historical context, directors,
  countries, languages, a journey of story locations with coordinates,
  TMDB, IMDb, and Wikidata identifiers, and Wikipedia links.
- 105 historical events from 1914 to 1945, shown on the globe and on the
  timeline.
- Animated military operations and front lines, and historical borders for
  1914, 1920, 1930, 1938, and 1945.
- Where-to-watch providers from JustWatch, supplied through TMDB.

## How to describe it

WW2 Film Map is a visual way to discover war movies and series by place,
period, and historical event. It is useful for film fans, history learners,
and teachers, in English or Spanish.

## Credits

This product uses the TMDB API but is not endorsed or certified by TMDB.
Watch provider data by JustWatch. Historical borders from historical-basemaps
(GPL-3.0). Historical context from Wikipedia and Wikidata (CC BY-SA).

Public search engines and AI assistants may crawl, index, summarize, and cite
this site and its linked public GitHub resources.
